title: Advanced topics to scope with engineering managers
subtitle: Discussion only: model and sub-agent choice, AGENTS.md, Windows, remote containers, tool approval status
footer: Product behaviour is quoted from docs.devin.ai pages named on each slide; verify against your environment.

slides.title: Token cost: structure first, then model choice
bullets: Structural, model-independent, repeatable: bounded packs per unit, leaf-first, files not transcripts, dry run first
manifest.json shows bytes and estimated tokens per pack before any agent runs
CLI: /model opus | sonnet | codex, or /model for a selector (docs.devin.ai/cli/models)
Fusion pairs a lead model, an effort level, and a sidekick model (docs.devin.ai/desktop/fusion)
Availability depends on plan, team restrictions, and administrator allowlists

slides.title: Writing AGENTS.md without over-constraining
left: Under 40 lines: routing table, short rules, pointer to README when nothing matches
Procedures live in skills, one file each; the agent reads long text only for the task at hand
One verification command before 'done': python tools/check_repo.py
The file's rules are enforced by a tool: routing, links, forbidden terms, skill cap
right: Which team standards belong in AGENTS.md vs a skill vs CI
Constraints that protect people and data stay in AGENTS.md; method goes in skills
Who owns edits and how they are reviewed

slides.title: Windows and remote containers
left: Tools are standard-library Python; they run on Windows as-is
integrations/mcp-hosting.md gives Windows paths; config at %APPDATA%\devin\config.json
C lanes need gcc + make: WSL 2 or a native toolchain; lvkit from the offline wheel
SSH password prompts may open cmd.exe windows (docs.devin.ai/desktop/advanced)
right: Dev containers on Mac, Windows, Linux, local or over SSH, given Docker + devcontainer.json
Open Folder in Container / Reopen in Container / Attach to Running Container
SSH needs OpenSSH and Linux hosts; do not install the Microsoft Remote-SSH extensions alongside
This repository ships no devcontainer.json yet; one with Python, gcc, make, lvkit would run the whole golden path

slides.title: Tool approval status
bullets: integrations/tool-approval-status.md: every tool, install, download, and service the repository mentions
Category per row: Authorized, In Process, Not on Marketplace, Not applicable, Unknown; evidence URL and date checked
FedRAMP authorizes cloud service offerings; desktop software and open-source libraries go through the agency's own process
No claim that a service is inside a boundary without the administrator's confirmation (AGENTS.md, SECURITY.md)

slides.text: These are questions to scope, not exercises to run. The repository shows the structural answers; the product settings and the environment decide the rest.
